item.title: Unusual circuits in the Intel 386's standard cell logic
item.description:
📝 The giant multiplexers The standard cell circuitry that I'm examining (red box above) is part of the control logic that selects registers while executing an instruction. Registers are specified with 7-bit control signals that select one of the 30 registers and control which part of the register is accessed. Instead, I'll discuss how the register control circuit uses multiplexers, implemented with standard cells.
🔗 Read more: https://www.righto.com/2025/11/unusual-386-standard-cell-circuits.html
